A LITTLE MORE ABOUT ME

Connecting dots.
Building forward.

I spent the last two years building a healthcare AI company on my own, from the first interviews with doctors and medical students to the product itself, and took it into two live pilots. Before that I co-founded an edtech company and closed it when the demand wasn't there. I'm now looking for a founding team to build with.

Current status: I have stopped working on Aivana Health Intelligence and the company is being formally wound down. I'm looking for what to build next, this time with a team.

The journey so far.

I care about what a result actually tells us. Interviews validate a problem; a prototype tests an idea; a pilot tests a workflow. Sustained adoption and revenue need their own evidence. This distinction guides how I build, measure and change direction.

Aug 2024 to 2026

Founder · Healthcare AI Product

Aivana Health Intelligence

Started venture development in 2024 and formally registered the company in 2025. Held 100+ conversations with doctors, hospital staff and students, plus 370+ medical-student validations during the Kaya pilot.

Built Kaya, a virtual AI patient for case-based learning, and ran a 1-week pilot at Yashwant Ayurvedic Medical College and Hospital. Evidence led to two product pivots toward tools for clinicians. Ran an 11-week pilot at Tulip Hospital with outpatient doctors across 371 consultations, combining differential diagnosis and clinical documentation. Final 3-day measurement: 91% note accuracy, about 20% less documentation time.

Researched 12 clinical AI vendors and created five institutional workflow demonstrations to support partner conversations.

MARCH — AUGUST 2026

Founder’s Office Associate · Growth & Operations

Dyadic Health

Aivana was bootstrapped. To extend its runway I joined Dyadic Health, an eldercare startup, as Founder's Office Associate for growth and operations from Mar 2026 to Aug 2026, and kept Aivana going part time.

Designed a shared CRM, KPI dashboards and SOPs for partner onboarding, customer coordination and launch execution. Reported founder review time fell from about 4 hours to 50 minutes per day, an approximately 80% review-time reduction.

Coordinated onboarding and operational readiness for 11 healthcare and eldercare partners. Built a 200+ member caregiver community, generated 35 discovery conversations and coordinated the first paid caregiver cohort’s launch.

Feb 2025 to Aug 2025

Co-Founder and COO

GnixarAcademy

Researched and prioritised 30+ academic institutions. Built an outreach sequence, qualification rubric and pilot-proposal templates, advancing several institutional conversations to proposal stage.

Procurement research showed weak willingness to pay, so I left rather than keep pushing.

Zangoh

Two companies I stopped

GnixarAcademy Feb 2025 to Aug 2025

As co-founder and COO I checked demand across 30+ institutions and built partner outreach. Procurement research showed weak willingness to pay, so I left rather than keep pushing.

Aivana 2024 to 2026

I bootstrapped Aivana and took the Dyadic role to fund it. The pilots showed the product could work in a hospital, but turning pilots into paid hospital contracts needed full-time selling, a longer runway and more hands than one founder funding it from a salary could give. I chose to stop cleanly rather than keep it running half-way. The main thing I took from it: I don't want to build alone again.

What I'd bring to a founding team

Because I ran Aivana alone, I have done every early-stage job at least once: finding users, building the product, getting an institution to say yes to a pilot, running it, and reading the results. In a team I'd take the business side: customers, pilots, partnerships and operations.

I have set up and run pilots directly with a medical college and a hospital in India, so I know what that process involves from the first meeting to the results.
